title: A 2,000-Year-Old Computer Pulled From the Sea
alt_titles: The Machine That Should Not Exist
Ancient Greeks Built a Computer. Then It Vanished.
description:
In 1901, sponge divers pulled a shapeless lump of corroded bronze and wood from a Roman-era shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera. For two years nobody looked at it twice. Then, on 17 May 1902, someone noticed a gear wheel inside the rock.

It turned out to be the most complex machine that survives from the ancient world: a hand-cranked bronze calculator, about the size of a shoebox, with at least 30 interlocking gears. It showed where the Sun and Moon would be, the phase of the Moon, the dates of eclipses, and even when the Olympic Games were due. Nothing comparable appears again for well over a thousand years.

This is the story of how it was found, how scientists spent a century decoding it with X-rays, gamma rays and CT scanners, and the flaw that has been hiding in plain sight all along.
